lesson.title: Database Indexing, B-Trees, and Query Plan Optimization
lesson.description: Master indexing mechanics: B-tree indexed lookup, composite indexes, column order, write cost overhead, EXPLAIN query plan analysis, and index trade-offs.
learning_objectives: Explain balanced-tree lookup and index maintenance tradeoffs
Choose and inspect composite indexes without universal planner claims
Read plans and distinguish index-only eligibility from zero heap fetches

summary: An index is a tradeoff, not a guarantee of a chosen plan.
Use explicit fixtures and correct catalog columns.
Index Only Scan can still require heap visibility checks.
interview_takeaways: State workload and selectivity before proposing an index.
Measure and explain the plan with visibility and write-cost limits.
common_mistakes: Filtering a table-name catalog column using an index name
Treating all update paths and physical writes as identical
Treating planner costs or index sizes as portable constants

exercises.title: Which pg_stat_user_indexes column identifies the index name?
exercises.prompt_markdown: Which pg_stat_user_indexes column identifies the index name?
hints: Identify the schema, rows and exact catalog fields named in the question.
Separate a logical guarantee from a data-dependent planner or storage observation.

content.assumptions: PostgreSQL; exact catalog-column names and visibility semantics; no universal planner-cost claim.
content.explanation: indexrelname names the index; relname names its table.

exercises.title: For (customer_id,order_date), describe the query pattern that directly uses the leading ke
exercises.prompt_markdown: For (customer_id,order_date), describe the query pattern that directly uses the leading key and explain the limitation.
hints: Identify the schema, rows and exact catalog fields named in the question.
Separate a logical guarantee from a data-dependent planner or storage observation.

content.reference_answer: Equality on customer_id followed by a range on order_date matches the ordering. Queries omitting the leading key are not universally impossible; inspect plan and cost for the engine version and data.

exercises.title: A sample creates an empty table and then promises a selected row
exercises.prompt_markdown: A sample creates an empty table and then promises a selected row. What must its fixture add?
hints: Identify the schema, rows and exact catalog fields named in the question.
Separate a logical guarantee from a data-dependent planner or storage observation.

content.reference_answer: Insert the exact row before querying, or change the expected result to empty. Declare schema, inserted data, query and ordering together; never invent a row in the answer.

exercises.title: What should a worked EXPLAIN example promise instead of a fixed cost or runtime?
exercises.prompt_markdown: What should a worked EXPLAIN example promise instead of a fixed cost or runtime?
hints: Identify the schema, rows and exact catalog fields named in the question.
Separate a logical guarantee from a data-dependent planner or storage observation.

content.reference_answer: Provide complete setup and ask the reader to inspect plan nodes, actual rows and visibility/heap behavior. State engine version and data. Timings and selected plans are observations, not universal expected constants.
